prompt: Hypothetical. Capital Rs 50,000, risk 1%, entry Rs 300, stop Rs 290, concentration cap 25%. How many whole shares does the plan allow?
solution: Risk budget = Rs 500. Risk per share = Rs 10. Raw shares = 50. Cash cap = floor(50,000 / 300) = 166. Concentration cap = floor(12,500 / 300) = 41. Shares = the minimum of 50, 166 and 41 = 41.

prompt: Hypothetical. You hold 50 shares bought at Rs 250. The stop trigger is Rs 240. The stop is a GTT market stop that stays live overnight. The price gaps down and the stop fills at Rs 232. What is the loss in rupees?
solution: Loss per share = 250 - 232 = Rs 18. Loss = 50 x 18 = Rs 900. Check: 50 x 250 = Rs 12,500 and 50 x 232 = Rs 11,600. The difference is Rs 900. The planned loss was Rs 500, so the gap added Rs 400.

prompt: Hypothetical. You hold 50 shares bought at Rs 250. A stop-loss order has trigger Rs 240 and limit Rs 238. The price trades at Rs 238 and the order fills there. What is the loss in rupees?
solution: Loss per share = 250 - 238 = Rs 12. Loss = 50 x 12 = Rs 600. Check: 50 x 250 = Rs 12,500 and 50 x 238 = Rs 11,900. The difference is Rs 600.

prompt: Hypothetical. You want your exit to leave your position once the trigger price is hit, even if the price falls fast. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A stop with a limit price always leaves once it is triggered, because the limit protects the exit price.
No stop type guarantees an exit. An SL-M sells at the best price available once triggered, but the fill can be far from the trigger. Circuit limits and market protection can also get in the way.
A limit buy order exits a long position at the trigger price.
A stop with a limit price makes the exit certain.

explanations.a: A limit price can stop the order from filling. If the price falls below the limit, the order may stay open. It does not make the exit certain.
explanations.c: A buy order adds shares. It does not exit a long position.
explanations.d: A limit price can stop the order filling. It does not make the exit certain.

prompt: Hypothetical. You plan to hold a delivery position for three weeks. Your order preview shows the intraday product. Which response is correct?

options.text: Submit it, because the intraday product is cheaper
Change the product to the delivery product before you submit, because the intraday product is for same-day trades
Submit it, then change the product in the holdings screen
Submit it, because the product makes no difference to a holding

explanations.a: Cost is not the test. The holding period decides the product. Intraday is for same-day trades, so a three-week plan does not fit it.
explanations.c: Changing the product after submission is not the fix. Check the product before you submit.
explanations.d: The product changes how the position is held and closed. It matters for a holding.

prompt: Spot the mistake in this order preview: "Buy 100 shares at Rs 250. Product: intraday. Plan: hold for three weeks. Stop: Rs 240." Which part is wrong?

options.text: The quantity of 100 shares
The intraday product, for a plan to hold three weeks
The stop at Rs 240
Nothing. the preview is correct

explanations.a: The quantity is a separate choice. It can be right or wrong, but the product is the clear error here.
explanations.c: A stop at Rs 240 is a valid level for this example. The error is the product.
explanations.d: The product does not fit a three-week hold, so the preview is not correct.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "My real order filled at Rs 250, so my stop at Rs 240 will fill at Rs 240." Which part is wrong?

options.text: The entry of Rs 250
The claim that a stop at the trigger always fills at the trigger
The stop level of Rs 240
Nothing. a stop always fills at its trigger

explanations.a: The entry is the price of the earlier fill. It is not the error.
explanations.c: A stop level is a choice, and Rs 240 is a valid level. The error is the claim about the fill.
explanations.d: A stop does not always fill at its trigger. After a gap, the fill can be far from the trigger, and a limit can stop the order filling at all.

prompt: Hypothetical. You hold 100 shares. You set a GTT sell order for 150 shares at Rs 240. What is the mistake?

options.text: The GTT is too far from the price
The GTT quantity is larger than the holding, so it cannot match what you own
A GTT cannot be used for a stop at all
GTT orders never expire, so there is no mistake to find

explanations.a: The price level is a plan choice. The quantity is the clear error here.
explanations.c: A GTT can hold a stop-type exit order. The problem in this example is the quantity.
explanations.d: A GTT does not last forever. It stays active for up to one year. Check the date as well as the quantity.
